guard: a connector seed whose `ext add` re-exec is refused journals nothing: no crash cursor, no staged payload, no pending child marker, so the next reconcile is not wedged
why: `seedOne` wrote its crash cursor, staged the payload and wrote the pending child marker, and only
then built the `ext add` argv with `selfArgv()`. Since #1629 that call can refuse, and the marker
is cleared only after the spawn, so a refusal left the cursor and the marker behind. Measured with
the real CLI entry afterwards: `cotal ext list` exited 1 with `a connector seed may be mid-flight`.
Every place the guard could slide back to has a mutant, each naming the record it would leave:
after the marker (the order #1641 shipped, graded on the retry), after the cursor, after the
staging, and the marker hoisted above the guard.

mutations.name: the entry is validated after the marker is written, as #1641 shipped it
mutations.cell: re-exec refused: the next reconcile meets the same refusal, not an interrupted seed
mutations.expectRed: re-exec refused: the next reconcile meets the same refusal, not an interrupted seed

mutations.name: the entry is validated after the cursor reaches phase add
mutations.cell: re-exec refused: no crash cursor is left for the next boot
mutations.expectRed: re-exec refused: no crash cursor is left for the next boot

mutations.name: the pending child marker is written before the entry is validated
mutations.cell: re-exec refused: no pending seed-child marker is left either
mutations.expectRed: re-exec refused: no pending seed-child marker is left either

mutations.name: the entry is validated after the payload is staged
mutations.cell: re-exec refused: no payload was staged
mutations.expectRed: re-exec refused: no payload was staged
